turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Krishnan, sorry about the delay. Please go in, doctor is free.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Good afternoon, doctor.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good afternoon. Do sit. What brings you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, for some months I have had bloating, and loose stools, after milk or ice cream.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): After milk or ice cream. How long, roughly?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Four months. Perhaps a little more. I hoped it would settle by itself.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it happen every time, or only now and then?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Nearly every time. A glass of milk in the evening, or ice cream when the grandchildren visit. Within an hour the tummy is full of gas, and the stools become loose.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any pain with the bloating?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Not sharp pain. A heavy, stretched discomfort. It eases once the loose stool has passed, mostly.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood in the stool? Or black stools?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. Nothing I could point to.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. So nothing definite. Any loss of weight?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Weight is unchanged. My clothes fit as they did last year.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever? Any vomiting?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, and no vomiting.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you cut out the dairy at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. For one week I avoided milk, curd, ice cream, everything. Tea without milk also.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And in that week, did the bloating and loose stools settle?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I suppose, a little. Sometimes, not really. We were at my sister's, so the meals were different. I cannot be sure.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will leave that as unclear, then. What medicines are you taking regularly?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipin in the morning for the pressure. I nearly said ten milligrams, but it is five milligrams. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, one small spoon stirred in warm water.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Go on.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol one at night. I think ten milligrams, though, err, the name has slipped my mind, the strip is at home. And my sugar tablets, metforman, 500 milligrams morning and night, for the sugar.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me set that out. Amlodipine five milligrams each morning for the pressure, and an Ayurvedic powder, one small spoon every morning. A cholesterol tablet at night, possibly ten milligrams, name forgotten, and metformin five hundred morning and night for the sugar. Is that fair?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. That is correct. I do not miss them.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines or foods?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None that I know of.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history — bowel disease, coeliac, or sugar?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had sugar, later in life. No bowel disease in the family, and I have not heard of coeliac among us.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Smoking? Alcohol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. Alcohol, only a small peg at weddings, not a habit.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still in work?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Retired now, from the accounts department of the electricity board. I live with my wife.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any burning or frequency when you pass urine?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Urine is quite normal.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, breathlessness?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Neither, doctor.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the couch for a moment. Abdomen is soft, bowel sounds are present, no tenderness, and I do not feel a mass.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Provisionally I would call this lactose intolerance, as it follows milk and ice cream and you have not lost weight. I still cannot rule out coeliac disease.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Please tell me what I should do.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am booking a blood test for coeliac disease, the tissue transglutaminase, today. Keep a diet diary for two weeks, what you eat and when the bloating or loose stools come. Carry on limiting milk and ice cream, but do not stop wheat or roti before the blood test, and do not stop the Ayurvedic powder.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Bring the cholesterol strip next time, so we can check the name and the dose. We will review in two weeks.
[SEG0044] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book that blood test downstairs just now, and the review appointment in two weeks. I will put the form in the queue.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you very much. I shall go down directly.

spec.situation: Person with bloating and loose stools after milk and ice cream for months, no weight loss; tried to avoid dairy for a week; blood test for coeliac planned; diet diary asked.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Night-time cholesterol tablet is current, but 10 mg is only guessed/possible, not confirmed.
bad.text: the cholesterol one (dose=10 mg, frequency=at night, indication=cholesterol, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Blood in stool or black stools was specifically asked about and not confirmed: patient said 'Sometimes, not really. Nothing I could point to,' and doctor summarised this as nothing definite.

The patient tried avoiding all dairy for one week, including milk, curd, ice cream and tea without milk, but the effect on symptoms was unclear because meals were different while visiting his sister; doctor agreed to leave this as unclear.
Abdominal discomfort was described as a heavy, stretched discomfort rather than sharp pain.
The patient stated he does not miss his regular medicines.
The recorded cholesterol tablet dose of 10 mg is wrong as a definite medication entry; the patient only thought it might be 10 mg and the name had slipped his mind.
